hero.headline: Supreme Court asked to reconsider Haitian immigration case
hero.teaser: Lawyers representing Haitian immigrants have requested the Supreme Court dismiss a case after new evidence emerged about how the Trump administration ended temporary protective status.
hero.body:
Attorneys representing Haitian immigrants have filed a motion asking the Supreme Court to dismiss a case, arguing that the court lacks a complete record of how the Trump administration decided to end temporary protective status for Haitians living in the United States.

Temporary protective status allows immigrants from countries experiencing armed conflict, natural disasters, or other extraordinary conditions to live and work legally in the United States. The Trump administration terminated this protection for Haitians, leading to legal challenges that have now reached the Supreme Court. The attorneys contend that newly discovered evidence is crucial to the case and that the court cannot make a fair decision without access to the full decision-making record.

The Supreme Court recently heard oral arguments in the consolidated case challenging the administration's effort to strip temporary protected status from hundreds of thousands of Haitian and Syrian immigrants. During the arguments, the conservative-leaning majority of justices appeared sympathetic to the Trump administration's position.

The Trump administration's solicitor general argued that the 1990 legislation establishing temporary protective status prevents courts from reviewing the Department of Homeland Security's decision to terminate the program. However, the lawyers representing Haitian and Syrian immigrants countered that the administration failed to follow proper legal procedures when ending the protections.

A federal judge in Washington, D.C. previously blocked the termination of temporary protective status for Haitians in February, citing racial animus as part of the motivation. During oral arguments, liberal justices raised concerns about whether the administration's decision was influenced by race, pointing to the president's past inflammatory statements about Haiti and other nations.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson questioned how the administration's discriminatory remarks should not be considered relevant to the case. The Trump administration argued those comments were taken out of context.

If the Supreme Court sides with the Trump administration, analysts say the administration would likely seek to end temporary protective status for all countries. Nearly 1.3 million people held temporary protective status when the second Trump administration began. Last year, the Supreme Court allowed the administration to strip temporary protected status from more than 300,000 Venezuelans through its emergency procedures.

The temporary protective status program, established in 1990, does not offer a pathway to citizenship but allows citizens from designated countries to remain and work in the United States if they cannot safely return home. The Department of Homeland Security has discretion to extend or terminate these designations.

The Supreme Court is expected to decide the case in late June or early July.

cards.headline: Iran says nuclear talks to begin Friday as US-Iran ceasefire takes hold
cards.body:
Iran announced that negotiations on nuclear arms and sanctions relief will begin Friday, following the signing of an initial ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran. The talks will commence immediately after both nations formalize the preliminary deal that has brought a pause to military hostilities.

Iran's foreign minister confirmed the timeline for the diplomatic negotiations, which represent a significant shift from weeks of military conflict between the two nations. The ceasefire agreement has already led to reduced fighting in Lebanon, though details of the arrangement remain disputed between the parties involved.

The terms of the ceasefire have become a point of contention. Iran maintains that the agreement requires Israeli forces to withdraw from Lebanon, a condition the country says is essential to the deal's implementation. US officials have downplayed the written text of the agreement, saying it does not fully capture commitments made through back-channel diplomatic communications. They describe the text as intentionally vague to allow for flexibility in implementation.

Hezbollah and Iran have clashed with the United States over what they characterize as unclear terms in the ceasefire deal. The ambiguity has left unanswered questions about enforcement and compliance, even as a relative quiet has settled over Lebanon. Iran's military has warned Israel of a strong response if it continues strikes in Lebanon despite the ceasefire.

The upcoming negotiations will be tested by deeper questions about Iran's willingness to engage with the United States. Protesters outside the foreign ministry in Tehran have demanded no return to talks with America, reflecting domestic skepticism about the agreement.

Sources with knowledge of previous negotiations point to significant communication breakdowns that contributed to the escalation into armed conflict. Misunderstandings about how Iran's complex nuclear programme functioned, including the purpose of key facilities and the scope of Iran's future nuclear plans, all played a role in the deterioration of talks.

The new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, has not clarified whether the fatwa banning the use of nuclear weapons set out by his late father remains in place. This uncertainty adds another layer of complexity to the upcoming negotiations, as calls inside Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon have inevitably grown following the conflict.

President Trump said he hopes to put the Iran war in the rearview mirror, signaling a desire to move past the conflict that has dominated recent weeks. The upcoming Friday talks will test whether the ceasefire can hold long enough for both nations to reach a broader agreement on Iran's nuclear program and the lifting of economic sanctions that have strained the Iranian economy for years.

Many Iranians remain focused on practical concerns rather than questions of victory, asking whether the deal will lower prices and reduce the fear of another war.

cards.headline: FBI disrupts planned attack on White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Authorities arrested multiple people in connection with an alleged plot to attack a UFC cage-fighting event at the White House using drones and guns.
cards.body:
Federal authorities disrupted a plot to attack a UFC event at the White House, charging five men in connection with the alleged scheme. According to court filings, the group planned to use snipers and drones in the attack.

The suspects allegedly expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers. A teenager was among those arrested in the case.

cards.headline: Eight killed in B-52 crash at Edwards Air Force Base in California
cards.body:
A Boeing B-52 Stratofortress bomber carrying eight people crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in the Mojave Desert during a test flight on Monday, killing everyone on board. The aircraft went down in a fiery explosion that sent thick plumes of smoke into the air at the base, located about 100 miles northeast of Los Angeles.

Flight tracking data shows the bomber made a sharp right turn after takeoff, followed by a near 180-degree turn before descending at approximately 5,056 feet per minute, nearly ten times the normal descent rate for landing preparation. The aircraft was supporting a radar modernization program when the crash occurred.

The eight victims included Boeing employees, government workers, military personnel, and civilian contractors. Two have been publicly identified as Lt. Col. Miles Middleton and Jeromy Smith, an engineer at the base. According to Smith's wife, he was "a leader" and "a hero."

According to Col James Hayes, the deputy commander for the 412th Test Wing at Edwards, the B-52 was equipped with a modernized radar system designed to keep the bomber operational through at least 2050, nearly a century after the aircraft first entered service in the 1950s.

Aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti, who previously investigated crashes for the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board, suggested the crash may have resulted from a flight control problem. "I think it was definitely a controllability issue," Guzzetti said. "Now, whether that was tied to an engine failure, a flight control failure, or some new testing device failure, I'm not sure."

He noted that issues could include controls rigged incorrectly after maintenance work, a catastrophic engine problem, or failure of equipment being tested.

The investigation into the cause could take up to six months to complete, officials said. The airfield remained closed as crews made the crash site safe for search and recovery teams. Fires flared up overnight at the scene, according to Mike Paoli, a spokesperson for the 412 Test Wing.

Edwards Air Force Base serves as a major testing facility for military aircraft. The 412th Test Wing conducts developmental testing of all Air Force aircraft, weapons systems, software, and components before purchase and throughout their operational lifespan.

This crash represents one of the more serious military aviation accidents in recent years. It comes as the Air Force continues to rely on its aging B-52 fleet, which remains a key component of American strategic military capabilities despite its decades of service. The military has maintained and upgraded the bombers over the years, though the fleet's advanced age presents ongoing maintenance and safety considerations.

cards.headline: California fault systems reach highest stress levels in 1,000 years
cards.body:
California's San Andreas and San Jacinto fault systems have accumulated tectonic stress to levels not seen in at least 1,000 years, according to research published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth. Scientists describe the region as existing in a "critically loaded state" with increased potential for a major earthquake.

Researchers from the University of Hawaii at Mānoa used computer models to analyze how stress builds and releases along these fault lines. They incorporated 1,000 years of earthquake history into their simulations to determine current stress levels across multiple fault segments. The findings reveal that stress is now at or above the highest values recorded over the past millennium.

"Our results show that stress levels on multiple fault segments are now at or above the highest values seen in the past millennium and that the region may be capable of a large through-going rupture involving both fault systems," said Liliane Burkhard, the lead author of the study.

One significant finding concerns Cajon Pass, located where the two fault systems meet. The research suggests this area functions as an "earthquake gate" that could either block large ruptures from traveling between faults or allow both systems to rupture simultaneously in a single event. Whether this gate opens or closes depends on how closely the stress levels on both fault systems align at the moment of rupture.

"Right now, with stress at historically high levels across the region and more than 160 years elapsed since the last major rupture, the system is in a critically loaded state," Burkhard explained. The last major earthquake on the San Andreas Fault occurred in 1857, while the San Jacinto Fault experienced its most recent significant event in 1918.

The accumulation of stress over more than a century means the region faces what scientists characterize as a heightened probability for a substantial seismic event. If both faults rupture together, the consequences could be severe across Southern California, given the densely populated areas near these fault systems.

However, the research does not predict when such an earthquake might occur. Instead, it establishes the geological conditions that make major seismic activity possible. Scientists stress that understanding these risk scenarios is essential for preparedness planning.

"What we can say is that the system is critically stressed, and that physics-based models like this one give us a clearer picture of the range of scenarios we should be prepared for," Burkhard said.

Researchers continue monitoring both fault systems using GPS networks, seismometers, and other instruments to track ground movement and identify any early warning signs. The findings underscore the ongoing seismic risks facing millions of residents living near these critical fault lines in Southern California.

cards.headline: Russian warship fired warning shots at British yacht in English Channel
cards.teaser: Russia confirmed that one of its naval vessels fired warning shots near a UK-flagged yacht sailing in the English Channel.
cards.body:
A Russian Navy warship fired warning shots near a British yacht in the English Channel. The incident involved a retired British couple who were sailing in the area. Russian authorities confirmed the incident occurred.

The couple told BBC Newsnight they attempted to change course before the shots were fired, trying to demonstrate their new direction to the warship. British officials launched an investigation into the encounter. The couple described the experience as surreal.

cards.headline: Trump offers conditional support to Ukraine at G7 summit
cards.teaser: President Trump signaled a potential shift in his approach to Ukraine during the G7 summit, though he attached conditions to any assistance.
cards.body:
At the G7 summit, President Trump repeated calls for a negotiated settlement to the Ukraine war, saying Moscow "should make a deal." He claimed to have spoken with both Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Russian President Putin on Sunday before the summit, stating both men were open to a meeting. Trump characterized the death toll as "ridiculous."

G7 allies worked to refocus Trump's attention on Ukraine after the Iran conflict had dominated his recent agenda. Trump previously lost patience with efforts to negotiate a deal requiring Ukraine to cede territory it still controls on the battlefield.

cards.headline: FBI says group planned sniper and drone attack on White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Federal authorities say a group planned to use snipers and drones to attack a UFC event at the White House.
cards.body:
The FBI has unsealed court filings revealing that a group allegedly plotted to attack a UFC event at the White House using snipers and drones. Federal authorities say they disrupted the plan before it could be carried out.

According to the documents, the group expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers. The Justice Department has announced charges against five men in connection with the alleged plot.

cards.headline: Trump offers conditional support to Ukraine at G7 summit
cards.teaser: President Trump signaled a potential shift in his approach to Ukraine during the G7 summit, though he attached conditions to any assistance.
cards.body:
At the G7 summit, President Trump repeated calls for a negotiated settlement to the Ukraine war, saying Moscow "should make a deal." He claimed to have spoken with both Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Russian President Putin on Sunday before the summit, stating both men were open to a meeting. Trump characterized the death toll as "ridiculous."

G7 allies worked to refocus Trump's attention on Ukraine after the Iran conflict had dominated his recent agenda. Trump previously lost patience with efforts to negotiate a deal requiring Ukraine to cede territory it still controls on the battlefield.

cards.headline: G7 leaders weigh giving trusted partners access to advanced AI models
cards.teaser: Leaders of the Group of Seven nations discussed allowing trusted partner countries access to cutting-edge artificial intelligence models developed in the United States.
cards.body:
G7 leaders held discussions about providing trusted partner nations with access to the most advanced AI models being developed in the United States, according to sources familiar with the talks. The conversations took place as executives from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google attended the summit.

A draft G7 statement singled out potential risks associated with artificial intelligence development and deployment. French President Macron concluded the G7 summit with AI-focused talks and a dinner with President Trump. Advocacy groups urged G7 leaders to prioritize protecting children from risks posed by AI systems.

cards.headline: Trump and Modi to meet as US-India relations face challenges
cards.teaser: President Trump and Indian Prime Minister Modi are set to meet more than a year after their last encounter, amid a series of setbacks in bilateral relations.
cards.body:
President Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet for the first time in more than a year, as the two nations work to reset relations that have faced multiple setbacks. Despite mutual praise between the two leaders, US relations with India have encountered a series of difficulties since they last met.

The meeting comes at a time when both leaders are seeking to address tensions that have emerged in the bilateral relationship. Observers are watching to see whether the personal rapport between Trump and Modi can help overcome the recent challenges and restore momentum to US-India cooperation.

cards.headline: Shark drags swimmer underwater off Sydney beach
cards.teaser: A woman was mauled by an 11-foot shark off a Sydney beach as a lifeguard paddled toward her screams.
cards.body:
An 11-foot shark attacked a swimmer off a Sydney beach, dragging her underwater as a lifeguard paddled toward her. The woman grabbed the lifeguard's paddleboard during the attack and lost her arm in the mauling.

Sydney authorities reopened the beach under heavy patrols following the incident. The attack has sparked renewed conversation among ocean swimmers about the inherent risks of swimming in waters inhabited by sharks.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors charge 15 in Minnesota with conspiracy, allege antifa ties
cards.teaser: The U.S. Attorney for Minnesota charged 15 protesters with conspiracy, alleging they obstructed ICE agents and have ties to antifa groups.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in Minnesota charged 15 people with conspiracy to impede or injure federal officers. The charges relate to their response to an immigration enforcement crackdown conducted earlier this year. U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen and Michael McCarthy, the special agent in charge of Homeland Security Investigations for Minnesota, announced the charges at a Minneapolis press conference on Tuesday.

Prosecutors claim the defendants were part of Minneapolis-based groups that violently oppose law enforcement. The charges allege the defendants worked together to interfere with federal immigration enforcement operations in the state.

cards.headline: One killed in shooting at Delaware hospital, suspect arrested in Philadelphia
cards.teaser: A shooting at Wilmington Hospital in Delaware left one person dead and another injured before the suspect was taken into custody in Philadelphia.
cards.body:
A shooting at Wilmington Hospital in Delaware left one person dead and another injured on Tuesday afternoon around 3:30 p.m. Police Chief Wilfredo Campos confirmed that two people were shot inside the medical facility.

The suspect was taken into custody in Philadelphia following the incident. Law enforcement from Delaware and Pennsylvania coordinated the response to apprehend the individual responsible for the shooting.

cards.headline: Gulf Coast faces flooding as system may become Tropical Storm Arthur
cards.teaser: Heavy rain is battering the Gulf Coast, with forecasters warning the weather system could develop into the first named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season.
cards.body:
A weather system bringing intense rainfall to the Gulf Coast could become Tropical Storm Arthur, potentially the first named storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season. The National Hurricane Center in Miami is monitoring the system as it moves across southern states including Texas and Louisiana this week.

Louisiana is already experiencing dangerous flash flooding as the system develops. Tropical storm warnings have been issued for parts of the region as forecasters track whether the system will strengthen into a named tropical storm.

cards.headline: Rick Jackson defeats Trump-backed candidate in Georgia Republican governor runoff
cards.teaser: Billionaire health executive Rick Jackson won the Republican nomination for Georgia governor, defeating the candidate endorsed by former President Trump.
cards.body:
Rick Jackson, a billionaire healthcare executive, won Georgia's Republican primary runoff for governor, defeating Trump-backed lieutenant governor Burt Jones. Jackson will face Democratic candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms in November's general election.

The race drew national attention as a test of Trump's influence over Republican voters in the competitive swing state. The campaign was contentious, marked by libel litigation and federal challenges to Georgia election law. In a related runoff, Republican voters also selected US Representative Mike Collins to challenge Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff in the midterm elections.

cards.headline: Mike Collins wins Georgia Republican Senate primary, will face Ossoff
cards.teaser: Mike Collins secured the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in Georgia and will challenge Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff in the general election.
cards.body:
Mike Collins won the Republican primary runoff for U.S. Senate in Georgia, defeating former football coach Derek Dooley. Collins led by 10 points with 55% of the vote counted. He will face Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff in the general election.

Collins secured Trump's endorsement, which analysts suggest helped him perform well among election-day voters. In the same election cycle, Georgia Republicans held a gubernatorial primary runoff, where voters rejected Trump's preferred candidate in an upset.

hero.headline: SpaceX Overtakes Amazon to Become Fifth Most Valuable Company
hero.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX has surpassed Amazon in market valuation to become the world's fifth most valuable company, days after its stock market debut. The milestone represents a remarkable achievement for the rocket manufacturer and satellite operator, which has captured investor enthusiasm following its initial public offering.

SpaceX shares rose 13 percent when trading opened on the Nasdaq index on Tuesday. At one point, the company's valuation climbed to $2.97 trillion, leapfrogging Amazon's $2.65 trillion valuation. By the close of trading, shares had moderated to approximately 5 percent gains, with SpaceX valued at just above $2.66 trillion. The company floated at $135 per share on Friday and has appreciated roughly 50 percent since the offering.

The surge in valuation comes as SpaceX announced a major acquisition. The company agreed to purchase Cursor, an artificial intelligence-powered coding application, for $60 billion. The deal represents SpaceX's effort to strengthen its AI capabilities through its xAI division, which Musk established as the parent company overseeing SpaceX, the social media platform X, and satellite internet provider Starlink.

SpaceX's financial performance reveals significant losses despite the market enthusiasm. The company lost $4.9 billion in 2025 on revenues of $18.7 billion. This contrasts sharply with Amazon, which posted revenues of $717 billion and net income of $78 billion during the same period.

Analysts view the Cursor acquisition strategically. Harrison Rolfes of PitchBook noted that owning a tool trusted by professional developers provides a faster path to enterprise AI revenue than competing in the underlying model development race. Matt Britzman, a senior analyst at Hargreaves Lansdown, called it a positive move given Cursor's impressive coding models relative to cost.

The acquisition addresses a fundamental challenge for Cursor. While the startup has attracted over 1 million users with its AI coding capabilities, it has been hampered by limited access to computing power. SpaceX's position as a datacentre owner allows it to provide the infrastructure Cursor needs to scale operations.

Gil Luria of DA Davidson suggested the purchase improves SpaceX's competitive standing against Anthropic and OpenAI in the frontier AI model race. He emphasised that Grok, SpaceX's AI model, requires a coding component for enterprise customers to use alongside rivals' offerings like Claude Code and Codex.

The acquisition will be funded through stock rather than IPO proceeds and is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman noted that SpaceX's high stock valuation creates an advantage, requiring fewer shares to complete large acquisitions.

Musk's ownership stake in SpaceX has made him the world's first trillionaire, with his fortune estimated between $1.1 trillion and $1.3 trillion, according to various valuations.

cards.headline: Justice Department Seeks to Block Pollution Lawsuit Against Musk Data Center
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has intervened in a lawsuit over air pollution from an Elon Musk data center, citing national security concerns.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has moved to dismiss an air pollution lawsuit filed against xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, over emissions from its data center operations. The DOJ argued that national security considerations require the court to halt the case, which was brought by the NAACP alleging violations of air quality regulations.

The Trump administration's intervention represents direct federal support for Musk's company in the environmental dispute. The Justice Department asked the court to throw out the case entirely rather than allowing it to proceed through normal legal channels.

cards.headline: Wall Street Awaits Federal Reserve Rate Decision
cards.teaser: Stock futures showed little movement as investors prepared for the Federal Reserve's interest rate announcement under new chair Kevin Warsh.
cards.body:
Stock futures held steady as Wall Street prepared for the Federal Reserve's rate decision, marking Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed to record levels above 52,000, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq showed more muted performance ahead of the central bank announcement.

Meanwhile, investors are shifting focus toward emerging investment themes. Asset managers are filing for new ETFs targeting artificial intelligence and companies dubbed the "MANGOS," signaling a broader market rotation away from previous market leaders.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO Calls for New Social Norms in AI Era
cards.teaser: Jensen Huang said society must develop new social norms to adapt to the age of artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told the Associated Press that society must establish new social norms as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly prevalent. His remarks come as Nvidia continues to lead the market for AI processors that power machine learning systems.

In related infrastructure developments, Coherent has begun construction on an expanded Texas facility to increase production of optical components used in AI systems. The Commerce Department's CHIPS Program issued a letter of intent to provide Coherent up to $50 million in support for expanding indium phosphide production, a material critical for advanced computing applications.

cards.headline: White House Anthropic Restrictions Renew Congressional AI Debate
cards.teaser: Congressional lawmakers returned to debating AI policy after the White House imposed restrictions on Anthropic, a leading AI research company.
cards.body:
Anthropic has suspended its new Claude Fable 5 AI tool following concerns from U.S. government officials about cybersecurity and hacking risks. The move has reignited Congressional debate over artificial intelligence regulation.

The suspension reflects broader tensions between AI companies and the Trump administration over security concerns and export controls. The incident underscores ongoing discussions in Congress about how to balance innovation in the AI sector with national security considerations.

cards.headline: Asset Managers File for ETFs Tracking AI and MANGOS Stocks
cards.teaser: US asset managers submitted applications for the first exchange-traded funds targeting AI companies and a new group of mega-cap stocks dubbed MANGOS.
cards.body:
Asset management firms have filed regulatory applications to launch exchange-traded funds focused on artificial intelligence companies and a newly defined group of mega-cap technology stocks. The filings reflect Wall Street's shift away from the "Magnificent Seven" framework toward new groupings that include recently public companies.

Investors are embracing labels like "FAB 10" and "MANGOS" to describe an expanded universe of large technology companies that now includes SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic alongside established public firms. The new ETF applications signal institutional interest in providing investors with diversified exposure to this evolving group of high-value technology companies.

cards.headline: China Restricts Citizens' Access to Global Markets
cards.teaser: Beijing has implemented new restrictions limiting how Chinese individuals can engage with global financial markets.
cards.body:
The Chinese government has tightened controls on capital flows by restricting the ways citizens can participate in international markets. The measures are designed to keep capital within China's borders as authorities seek greater control over cross-border financial activity.

The restrictions represent Beijing's latest effort to manage capital outflows and maintain stability in domestic financial markets. The policy changes limit individual Chinese investors' ability to move money into foreign assets and participate in overseas investment opportunities.

cards.headline: Cockroaches carry thousands of bacterial gene fragments
cards.teaser: Researchers found cockroaches harbor thousands of pieces of bacterial genomes, demonstrating gene transfer across species extends beyond microbes.
cards.body:
Scientists have discovered that cockroaches carry thousands of fragments of bacterial genomes within their bodies, providing new evidence that gene transfer between species is not limited to microorganisms. The finding reveals a previously unknown aspect of how genetic material moves between different forms of life.

The research shows that transferring genes across species boundaries occurs more broadly in nature than previously understood. While horizontal gene transfer has been well documented in bacteria and other microbes, the extent to which it occurs in insects represents a significant scientific finding.

cards.headline: Scientists detect wind from Milky Way's central black hole
cards.teaser: Astronomers have detected wind blowing from Sagittarius A, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
cards.body:
Astronomers have detected powerful winds emanating from Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way. This discovery reveals a previously missing feature of the black hole and represents a significant finding for understanding these cosmic objects.

The detected winds travel at roughly 323 million kilometers per hour—about 30 percent of light speed—making them the fastest black hole winds ever recorded. The winds have carved out a cavity spanning three light years across. This detection offers new insights into how supermassive black holes influence their surrounding environments.

cards.headline: Amazon relies on European rockets as US alternatives lag
cards.teaser: Among the new large rockets Amazon planned to use for its satellite network, only Europe's Ariane 6 has delivered on schedule.
cards.body:
Amazon's satellite internet plans depend heavily on European launch providers after delays from other rocket developers. Arianespace has become a key partner, with its Ariane 6 rocket delivering on schedule when other large rockets Amazon contracted have not yet materialized.

The company is preparing to launch 36 satellites using an upgraded Ariane 6 variant scheduled for June 17. This mission will carry the heaviest payload in Ariane's history and debut the rocket's upgraded boosters, allowing Amazon to advance its satellite constellation despite setbacks from other providers.

cards.headline: Trump administration moves to block lawsuit over xAI gas turbines
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is attempting to block a Clean Air Act lawsuit filed by the NAACP against xAI over gas turbines.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has taken steps to block a lawsuit filed by the NAACP under the Clean Air Act targeting xAI's use of gas turbines. The civil rights organization alleges that xAI operates gas turbines without the required environmental permits for its data center supporting the Grok artificial intelligence system.

The lawsuit centers on whether xAI obtained proper Clean Air Act permits before operating the turbines. The NAACP contends the company is running the gas-powered equipment in violation of federal environmental regulations designed to limit air pollution.

cards.headline: Apple to move Hide My Email feature to different domain
cards.teaser: Apple plans changes to its Hide My Email privacy feature that could reduce its effectiveness by moving anonymously generated email addresses to a different domain.
cards.body:
Apple announced it will move its Hide My Email privacy feature to a different domain in the coming weeks. The change affects how the system generates anonymous email addresses for users who want to shield their real email addresses from apps and websites.

Security researchers have indicated the domain change could make the privacy feature less effective at protecting user identities. Hide My Email currently allows users to create randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to their actual inbox without revealing their real address.

cards.headline: Anthropic pauses planned billing changes for Claude Agent SDK
cards.teaser: Anthropic has paused its plan to switch to token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK after the change would have significantly increased costs for power users.
cards.body:
Anthropic halted plans to implement token-based billing for its Claude Agent software development kit. The company had originally scheduled the pricing change for implementation but paused the rollout after concerns emerged about the impact on users.

The planned billing model would have substantially increased costs for power users who rely heavily on the SDK. Anthropic has not announced when or if it will proceed with the token-based billing structure.

hero.headline: Golden Knights part ways with coach John Tortorella after Cup Final run
hero.teaser: John Tortorella will not return as head coach despite leading Vegas to the Stanley Cup Final after taking over with eight games left in the season.
hero.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights have decided that John Tortorella will not continue as their head coach beyond this season. Tortorella arrived late in the regular season with just eight games remaining and successfully led the team through a playoff run that culminated in a Stanley Cup Final appearance.

The move concludes Tortorella's time with the franchise after a brief but notable stint. He took on the coaching position when the season was winding down and managed to spark an unexpected postseason surge for the Golden Knights. The team's path to the championship series represents a significant achievement given the circumstances of his hiring.

With Tortorella's departure confirmed, the Golden Knights organization must now shift focus to identifying and hiring their next head coach before the start of the upcoming season. The team will conduct a comprehensive search to find someone capable of building on the momentum created during the recent playoff run.

Tortorella's ability to take over a team mid-season and guide them to the Stanley Cup Final demonstrated his coaching acumen and ability to quickly establish himself with a new roster. Despite the successful playoff performance, the organization determined that a change in leadership would be preferable moving forward.

The decision reflects a broader trend in professional sports where coaching changes occur even after successful seasons. The Golden Knights' front office evidently believes that pursuing a different direction will better serve the franchise's long-term objectives.

The timing of Tortorella's hiring, coming so late in the regular season, presented unique challenges and opportunities. He managed to implement his system and philosophy quickly enough to make a meaningful impact during the playoffs. However, the organization likely felt that beginning fresh with a coach from the outset of a season would be more beneficial.

Tortorella brought significant head coaching experience to Vegas, having previously led teams in multiple leagues throughout his long career. His recent success with the Golden Knights' roster proved he could connect with players and establish effective strategies rapidly. Nonetheless, the franchise has concluded that seeking a new coach represents the best path forward.

The Golden Knights have now entered a new phase, one that will require evaluating potential coaching candidates who can maintain or exceed the standard that Tortorella set during his playoff run. The organization will need to identify a coach who can build continuity with the existing roster while implementing a system that keeps the team competitive in the Western Conference.

As Vegas begins this search, they will be hoping to find a coach capable of developing the team's talent and sustaining their push toward championship contention. The bar has been set high by the recent Stanley Cup Final appearance, and the new coach will be tasked with meeting or surpassing those expectations when the season begins.

cards.headline: Mbappé becomes France's all-time leading scorer in World Cup win
cards.teaser: Kylian Mbappé scored twice in France's opening match to set a new national record and surpass Lionel Messi on the World Cup scoring charts.
cards.body:
Kylian Mbappé scored two goals in France's 3-1 victory over Senegal in their Group I opener on Tuesday, becoming France's all-time leading goalscorer in the process. The pair of goals also moved Mbappé ahead of Lionel Messi on the all-time World Cup scoring charts.

France's win gave them three points to start their World Cup campaign. Mbappé's performance continued his strong form at the international level and cemented his place in French football history. Senegal scored once in the match but could not overcome the French attack.

cards.headline: Knicks championship clincher draws largest Game 5 audience since 1998
cards.teaser: The Knicks' first NBA title in 53 years attracted 24.5 million viewers on Saturday night, the most-watched Game 5 in nearly three decades.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks' 94-90 victory over the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday night drew 24.5 million average viewers across ABC and ESPN, making it the most-watched Game 5 of an NBA Finals since 1998. The broadcast peaked at 33 million viewers during the game's final moments.

The championship victory marked the Knicks' first NBA title in 53 years.

cards.headline: Messi ties World Cup goal record with hat trick in Argentina win
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored three goals in Argentina's World Cup group stage match against Algeria on Tuesday night, tying the all-time record for most men's World Cup .
cards.body:
Lionel Messi made history on Tuesday night by scoring a hat trick against Algeria in the World Cup group stage, tying Miroslav Klose's all-time record of 16 men's World Cup goals. The three-goal performance gave Argentina a commanding 3-0 lead, and Messi was substituted late in the second half.

The victory marked a significant milestone in Messi's storied career and put Argentina in a strong position in Group I. The match took place during an exciting day of World Cup group stage play featuring several of the tournament's biggest stars.

cards.headline: Broncos excuse linebacker from camp following domestic violence arrests
cards.teaser: Denver excused Jonathon Cooper from mandatory minicamp after the outside linebacker was arrested twice in seven days on multiple charges.
cards.body:
The Denver Broncos excused outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from their mandatory minicamp this week. Cooper was arrested twice within a seven-day period and faces multiple domestic violence charges, including one felony count.

The team kept Cooper away from the scheduled minicamp while his legal matters proceed.

cards.headline: Pereira accuses Gane of illegal blows in UFC loss
cards.teaser: Alex Pereira released a statement claiming Ciryl Gane landed illegal strikes to the back of his head at UFC Freedom 250.
cards.body:
Alex Pereira released a statement Tuesday accusing Ciryl Gane of landing illegal blows to the back of his head during their UFC Freedom 250 fight. Pereira also criticized referee Herb Dean for failing to prevent the strikes.

The allegations came following Pereira's loss to Gane at the event. Pereira contended that the blows violated UFC rules and that Dean should have stopped them during the bout.

cards.headline: FBI thwarts planned attack targeting UFC event at White House
cards.teaser: Federal agents stopped a planned terror attack against members of Congress attending a UFC event at the White House on Sunday.
cards.body:
The FBI prevented a planned attack on a UFC event at the White House where members of Congress were present. According to newly unsealed court filings, five men have been charged in connection with the alleged plot.

The group allegedly planned to use snipers and drones in their attack. A mother's concerns about her teenage son led to the discovery of the plot, enabling authorities to stop it before it could be carried out. The event proceeded without incident.

hero.headline: Rapper Mystikal Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Rape
hero.body:
Louisiana rapper Mystikal, whose legal name is Michael Tyler, pleaded guilty to third-degree rape in connection with a 2022 arrest. The 55-year-old musician faces up to 20 years in prison following his guilty plea entered in a state courthouse outside Baton Rouge.

Tyler was originally charged with more serious offenses, including first-degree rape, simple robbery, domestic abuse battery, and false imprisonment. He initially pleaded not guilty to these charges. The guilty plea represents a deal that significantly reduced the severity of the case. Had he been convicted on the original charges, he would have faced mandatory life imprisonment.

The case centered on a victim who reported that Tyler raped her, beat her, and choked her. According to investigators, he also took her phone and car keys to prevent her from leaving and forced her to send him money through Cash App. His sentencing hearing was tentatively scheduled for June.

Tyler's recent conviction adds to a lengthy history of legal troubles. In 2004, he was sentenced to six years in prison after being found guilty of sexual assault and extortion involving his hairstylist. That conviction required him to register as a sex offender. In 2012, he spent three months in jail following an arrest on a misdemeanor domestic abuse charge. In 2017, he was charged with rape and kidnapping, though authorities ultimately dropped that case.

The rapper achieved commercial success during his career, scoring a global hit in 2000 with "Shake Ya Ass." The song was featured in the film "About a Boy" and earned him two Grammy nominations. His debut album reached the top of the Billboard 200 chart before his legal troubles derailed his career momentum.

Third-degree rape charges under Louisiana law carry serious penalties. The guilty plea allowed the case to proceed to sentencing without requiring a trial. The court's decision reflects the severity of the offense under state statutes.

Tyler's case reflects broader discussions about accountability within the entertainment industry. In recent years, numerous entertainment figures have faced criminal consequences for sexual offenses. His guilty plea came just days before a scheduled trial date of March 30.

The musician was represented by legal counsel throughout the proceedings as the case moved through Louisiana's criminal justice system. The guilty plea arrangement appears to have been negotiated to resolve the matter without proceeding to trial on the more serious charges initially brought against him.

cards.headline: Toy Story 5 Projected to Open With $275 Million Globally
cards.teaser: The latest Pixar sequel is expected to set a franchise box office record with its opening weekend.
cards.body:
Toy Story 5 is tracking toward a $275 million global opening weekend, the highest debut in the franchise's history. The film features a new antagonist: a tablet device called Lilypad that threatens the traditional toys' existence.

The Guardian's review criticizes the film for lacking novelty and passion despite its technical polish. The critic notes that while the movie addresses how addictive tech devices undermine imaginative play, it ultimately undermines its own premise by portraying the tablet character as capable of heroic self-sacrifice.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen, U2, Stevie Wonder to Perform at Obama Presidential Center Opening
cards.teaser: Major music stars will perform at the grand opening celebration of the center in Chicago.
cards.body:
The Obama Presidential Center will celebrate its grand opening on Chicago's South Side with performances by Bruce Springsteen, U2, and Stevie Wonder. The event takes place on the eve of Juneteenth, marking the unveiling of a monument to Barack Obama's legacy.

The center features commissioned original works by 30 artists from diverse backgrounds—a scale of artistic curation unprecedented at a presidential library. The Obamas' bold approach to the $850 million facility emphasizes cultural celebration and artistic vision alongside historical memorabilia for visitors.

cards.headline: Asia-Pacific Screen Economy Projected to Reach $200 Billion by 2031
cards.teaser: The regional entertainment market is expected to grow from $179 billion in 2026 to $200 billion within five years.
cards.body:
The Asia-Pacific screen economy is projected to reach $179 billion in 2026 and $200 billion by 2031, according to Media Partners Asia executive director Vivek Couto, who shared the figures at the APOS 2026 conference.

Couto characterized this growth as structural reallocation rather than simple expansion. The analysis points to a significant monetization gap currently defining the region's entertainment industry, with revenue and business models shifting substantially across Asia-Pacific.

cards.headline: The Pitt and The Simpsons Win at Rockie Awards
cards.teaser: The Banff World Media Festival announced winners for its international program competition.
cards.body:
The Pitt, The Simpsons, The Chair Company, and Mountainhead were among the winners at the 2026 Rockie Awards International Program Competition. The awards ceremony took place at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel in Banff, Alberta, Canada.

Allana Harkin, known for her work on Full Frontal With Samantha Bee, hosted the event. The Rockie Awards recognize excellence in international television programming and are presented annually at the Banff World Media Festival.

cards.headline: Hayley Kiyoko Makes Directorial Debut With Girls Like Girls
cards.teaser: The pop singer adapted her 2015 viral music video into a feature film exploring adolescent lesbian desire.
cards.body:
Pop singer Hayley Kiyoko made her directorial debut with Girls Like Girls, expanding her 2015 viral song into a feature film. The original track brought explicit lesbian desire into mainstream pop with its memorable hook, and the accompanying music video told a compressed narrative that now forms the basis of the full-length movie.

Critics have praised Kiyoko's directorial work as warmly assured, highlighting the film's exploration of adolescent yearning and desire. The adaptation represents an unusual journey from hit song to cinema.

cards.headline: HBO Actress Submits Herself for Emmy After Network Passes
cards.teaser: Brittany Allen self-submitted for Emmy consideration for her role as a dying cancer patient on The Pitt.
cards.body:
Brittany Allen submitted herself for Emmy consideration after HBO did not include her in its official submissions for The Pitt. She played a dying cancer patient on the medical drama and learned through her former publicist that she would not be part of the network's Emmy campaign.

Allen, who lives in Pasadena with her husband and 3-year-old son, said give me a call back, HBO when discussing the situation.

hero.headline: Supreme Court asked to reconsider Haitian immigration case
hero.teaser: Lawyers representing Haitian immigrants have requested the Supreme Court dismiss a case after new evidence emerged about how the Trump administration ended temporary protective status.
hero.body:
Attorneys representing Haitian immigrants have filed a motion asking the Supreme Court to dismiss a case, arguing that the court lacks a complete record of how the Trump administration decided to end temporary protective status for Haitians living in the United States.

Temporary protective status allows immigrants from countries experiencing armed conflict, natural disasters, or other extraordinary conditions to live and work legally in the United States. The Trump administration terminated this protection for Haitians, leading to legal challenges that have now reached the Supreme Court. The attorneys contend that newly discovered evidence is crucial to the case and that the court cannot make a fair decision without access to the full decision-making record.

The Supreme Court recently heard oral arguments in the consolidated case challenging the administration's effort to strip temporary protected status from hundreds of thousands of Haitian and Syrian immigrants. During the arguments, the conservative-leaning majority of justices appeared sympathetic to the Trump administration's position.

The Trump administration's solicitor general argued that the 1990 legislation establishing temporary protective status prevents courts from reviewing the Department of Homeland Security's decision to terminate the program. However, the lawyers representing Haitian and Syrian immigrants countered that the administration failed to follow proper legal procedures when ending the protections.

A federal judge in Washington, D.C. previously blocked the termination of temporary protective status for Haitians in February, citing racial animus as part of the motivation. During oral arguments, liberal justices raised concerns about whether the administration's decision was influenced by race, pointing to the president's past inflammatory statements about Haiti and other nations.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson questioned how the administration's discriminatory remarks should not be considered relevant to the case. The Trump administration argued those comments were taken out of context.

If the Supreme Court sides with the Trump administration, analysts say the administration would likely seek to end temporary protective status for all countries. Nearly 1.3 million people held temporary protective status when the second Trump administration began. Last year, the Supreme Court allowed the administration to strip temporary protected status from more than 300,000 Venezuelans through its emergency procedures.

The temporary protective status program, established in 1990, does not offer a pathway to citizenship but allows citizens from designated countries to remain and work in the United States if they cannot safely return home. The Department of Homeland Security has discretion to extend or terminate these designations.

The Supreme Court is expected to decide the case in late June or early July.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Idaho transgender bathroom ban
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled Tuesday that Idaho cannot enforce a new law making it a crime for transgender individuals to use bathrooms that do not correspond with the.
cards.body:
A federal judge ruled Tuesday that Idaho cannot enforce a new law making it a crime for transgender individuals to use bathrooms that do not correspond with their sex assigned at birth. U.S. District Judge Amanda Brailsford of the District of Idaho granted a preliminary injunction in response to a legal challenge against the law.

The injunction temporarily prevents Idaho from enforcing the bathroom restriction while the case proceeds through the courts. The law would have criminalized transgender people for using facilities aligned with their gender identity rather than their biological sex at birth.

The ruling represents a significant development in ongoing legal battles over transgender rights across multiple states. Similar bathroom access laws have faced court challenges in other jurisdictions, with judges weighing claims about privacy, safety, and constitutional protections for transgender individuals.

Idaho has pursued multiple pieces of legislation affecting transgender residents in recent years. The state previously passed laws restricting transgender athletes from competing on sports teams matching their gender identity and limiting gender-affirming medical care for minors. Many of these measures have faced legal scrutiny.

The preliminary injunction will remain in effect while the court considers the full merits of the case. Judge Brailsford's decision means the state cannot prosecute anyone under the bathroom ban during this period. The ruling does not represent a final judgment on whether the law violates constitutional protections, but indicates the judge found sufficient legal questions to warrant blocking enforcement while litigation continues.

cards.headline: Trump-backed Moore wins Alabama Senate Republican runoff
cards.teaser: Rep. Barry Moore defeated his opponent in the Republican Senate runoff in Alabama, securing President Trump's endorsement in another primary victory.
cards.body:
Rep. Barry Moore won the Republican runoff election for U.S. Senate in Alabama, according to Decision Desk HQ projections. Moore received President Trump's endorsement and will advance to face the Democratic nominee in November's general election.

The victory marks another primary win for Trump this cycle as he continues backing candidates across Republican contests nationwide. Moore, currently serving in the House of Representatives, will compete for the Senate seat in the general election.

cards.headline: Jackson defeats Trump-backed Jones in Georgia governor runoff
cards.teaser: Healthcare executive Rick Jackson upset Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in the Republican gubernatorial runoff, handing President Trump a major primary loss in Georgia.
cards.body:
Georgia Republicans rejected President Trump's preferred candidate in the gubernatorial runoff, selecting billionaire healthcare executive Rick Jackson over Lt. Gov. Burt Jones. Despite endorsements from both Trump and Gov. Brian Kemp, Jones fell short in the upset victory.

Jackson will face Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms in November. In the same day's Republican runoff elections, voters also chose U.S. Representative Mike Collins to challenge Sen. Jon Ossoff in the Senate race.

cards.headline: Collins wins Georgia Senate runoff to challenge Ossoff
cards.teaser: Rep. Mike Collins defeated Derek Dooley in the Republican Senate runoff and will face Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in November.
cards.body:
Rep. Mike Collins won Georgia's Republican Senate runoff, defeating former football coach Derek Dooley with 55 percent of the vote. Collins had secured Trump's endorsement following the May primary.

Collins will advance to face incumbent Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in November's general election. The seat is considered competitive and strategically important for Republican efforts to maintain Senate control.

cards.headline: Oklahoma governor primary heads to runoff between Drummond and Mazzei
cards.teaser: Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond and President Trump's pick Mike Mazzei will compete in a runoff for the Republican gubernatorial nomination.
cards.body:
The Republican primary for governor of Oklahoma will proceed to a runoff between Attorney General Gentner Drummond and Mike Mazzei, who received President Trump's endorsement, according to Decision Desk HQ. Neither candidate secured enough votes to win the nomination outright in the initial primary.

The race will determine who succeeds term-limited Gov. Kevin Stitt. Polling ahead of the primary suggested Drummond might have an edge in the crowded field, though Mazzei also showed competitive standing. The runoff will decide the Republican nominee for the November general election.

cards.headline: Pastors for Trump founder advances to Oklahoma House runoff
cards.teaser: Jackson Lahmeyer and state Rep. Mark Tedford will compete in a runoff for the Republican nomination in Oklahoma's 1st Congressional District.
cards.body:
Jackson Lahmeyer, founder of Pastors for Trump, and Oklahoma state Rep. Mark Tedford advanced to a runoff in the GOP primary for Oklahoma's 1st Congressional District, according to Decision Desk HQ projections. Neither candidate cleared the 50 percent threshold needed to win the nomination outright.

Ten Republican candidates competed for the seat in the initial primary. The runoff will determine who becomes the Republican nominee for the November general election in the district.
